subproblem.title: Blow-up integrals over a set of zero n-density vanish (error term of Simon Ch. 3, proof of Thm 1.6 ⇒)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} (= Amb n ℓ), Hⁿ = μHE[n], and S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} an arbitrary set (no measurability or finiteness assumed). Suppose Hⁿ(S ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 in [0, ∞] as r ↓ 0 (B_r(x) the closed ball, rⁿ read as ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ)). Then for every compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ (f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ)), ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dHⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) is Simon's blow-up map (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r) and the integral is the Bochner integral over Hⁿ restricted to η_{x,r}(S).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (x : Amb n ℓ) (S : Set (Amb n ℓ)), Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (S ∩ closedBall x r) / ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → ∀ f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Amb n ℓ) ℝ, Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' S, f y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, printed proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' — the estimate |∫_{η_{x,λ}(M∖N_j)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·Hⁿ(B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,λ}(M∖N_j)) = sup|f|·λ^{−n}·Hⁿ(B_{λR}(x) ∩ M∖N_j) → 0 — i.e. step 3 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary set S whose n-density at x tends to 0 (the parent proof applies it to S = A∖N and S = N∖A). Documented erratum: Simon prints the error set as 'M∖N_j', whereas his decomposition needs the estimate for M∖M_j and N_j∖M_j; since S is arbitrary here, this lemma covers both corrected error sets.

Notation. μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ; B_ρ(y) is the closed ball (Metric.closedBall); η_r := η_{x,r} = Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x); 'r ↓ 0' means along the filter 𝓝[>] 0; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal. Hypothesis (D): μ(S ∩ B_s(x))/ofReal(sⁿ) → 0 in [0, ∞] as s ↓ 0. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ) (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap); we show ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ → 0 as r ↓ 0.

Proof.
1. Support radius and sup bound. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ. Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0. If y ∉ B_R(0) then f(y) = 0: otherwise y ∈ support f ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) ⊆ B_R(0). Since f is continuous with compact support it is bounded: fix C ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| ≤ C for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
2. Scaling of Hⁿ under η_r (r > 0). For every T ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, μ(η_r(T)) = ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ · μ(T). Indeed η_r = h ∘ τ with τ(y) = y − x and h the homothety with center 0 and ratio r⁻¹ ≠ 0. τ is an isometry, so μ(τ(T)) = μ(T) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and μ(h(T')) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ · μ(T') = ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ · μ(T') because r⁻¹ > 0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). (This is SimonGMT Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_image; it is re-derived from Mathlib because Chapter04 is outside the frozen import closure of GMT.Ch05.Submission.)
3. Ball identity (r > 0). For every y, |η_r(y)| = r⁻¹|y − x| ≤ R ⟺ |y − x| ≤ rR, i.e. η_r(y) ∈ B_R(0) ⟺ y ∈ B_{rR}(x). Hence B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S) = η_r(S ∩ B_{rR}(x)), and by step 2, μ(B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S)) = ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ · μ(S ∩ B_{rR}(x)).
4. Density form. Define g(r) := ofReal(Rⁿ) · (μ(S ∩ B_{rR}(x)) / ofReal((rR)ⁿ)) ∈ [0, ∞]. For r > 0, ofReal((rR)ⁿ) = ofReal(rⁿ)·ofReal(Rⁿ) with both factors in (0, ∞), and ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ = ofReal(rⁿ)⁻¹. Therefore, in [0, ∞], g(r) = ofReal(Rⁿ)·ofReal(Rⁿ)⁻¹ · (ofReal(rⁿ)⁻¹ · μ(S ∩ B_{rR}(x))) = ofReal(rⁿ)⁻¹ · μ(S ∩ B_{rR}(x)) = μ(B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S)), using ofReal(Rⁿ)·ofReal(Rⁿ)⁻¹ = 1 and step 3.
5. g(r) → 0 as r ↓ 0. The map r ↦ rR is continuous, equals 0 at r = 0 and maps (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) since R > 0; hence it tends from 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0. Composing with (D): μ(S ∩ B_{rR}(x))/ofReal((rR)ⁿ) → 0 as r ↓ 0. Multiplying by the finite constant ofReal(Rⁿ) (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul) gives g(r) → ofReal(Rⁿ)·0 = 0. In particular, as 0 < ∞, g(r) < ∞ for all sufficiently small r > 0.
6. Estimate. Let r > 0 with g(r) < ∞ and put ν := μ.restrict(η_r(S)), so ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ = ∫ f dν. As f = 0 off B_R(0), ∫ f dν = ∫_{B_R(0)} f dν (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). B_R(0) is closed, hence measurable, so ν(B_R(0)) = μ(B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S)) = g(r) < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply and step 4). Since |f| ≤ C, norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const gives |∫_{B_R(0)} f dν| ≤ C · ν(B_R(0)).toReal = C · g(r).toReal. Hence |∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ| ≤ C · g(r).toReal for all sufficiently small r > 0. (This is Simon's display |∫_{η(S)} f| ≤ sup|f|·Hⁿ(B_R(0) ∩ η(S)) = sup|f|·λ^{−n}·Hⁿ(B_{λR}(x) ∩ S).)
7. Conclusion. By step 5 and continuity of toReal at 0 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), g(r).toReal → 0, so C · g(r).toReal → 0. By step 6 and the squeeze theorem for norms (squeeze_zero_norm'), ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dHⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0. Since f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ) was arbitrary, the theorem follows. ∎
Remarks: no measurability or finiteness of S is used (only closed balls are fed to Measure.restrict_apply, and μ is applied to arbitrary sets as an outer measure); the case n = 0 needs no change (ofReal(s⁰) = 1). Steps 2–4 are routine and are carried out inline (as `have`s) in the single theorem: the problem policy requires every new named helper to be its own DAG node.
proof_key_steps: Choose R > 0 with f = 0 off B_R(0) and C with |f| ≤ C (compact support, continuity)
Scaling Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(T)) = ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(T) (translation isometry + homothety) and ball identity B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(S) = η_{x,r}(S ∩ B_{rR}(x))
Hⁿ(B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(S)) = g(r) := ofReal(Rⁿ)·Hⁿ(S ∩ B_{rR}(x))/ofReal((rR)ⁿ), and g(r) → 0 by the density hypothesis composed with r ↦ rR
|∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dHⁿ| ≤ C·g(r).toReal for small r > 0 (f vanishes off B_R(0); finite-measure sup bound)

audit.reason: The prose and standalone one-line proposition agree, including arbitrary S and n = 0. All seven proof steps are justified: compact support supplies the radius and bound; scaling and the ball identity hold without measurability of S; positive finite factors justify ENNReal cancellation; density convergence gives eventual finiteness; measurable-ball restriction yields the integral bound; toReal continuity and squeezing finish. No missing hypothesis, circular reliance, or typeclass ambiguity occurs. The name is bare and unreserved.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent spaces are unchanged by zero-density modifications (pointwise Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2))
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ} (= Amb n ℓ), A, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} Borel sets with Hⁿ(A) < ∞ and Hⁿ(N) < ∞, x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Suppose Hⁿ((A ∖ N) ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 and Hⁿ((N ∖ A) ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 in [0, ∞] as r ↓ 0 (B_r(x) closed ball, rⁿ read as ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ)), and Q is the approximate tangent space of N at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q: finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(N)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ)). Then Q is the approximate tangent space of A at x (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (A N : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (x : Amb n ℓ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet N → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) A < ⊤ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) N < ⊤ → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) ((A \ N) ∩ closedBall x r) / ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) ((N \ A) ∩ closedBall x r) / ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 3, printed proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' (and Remark 1.5(2)) at a single point x: the decomposition ∫_{η(M)} = ∫_{η(N_j)} − ∫_{η(N_j∖M_j)} + ∫_{η(M∖M_j)}, the limit ∫_{η(N_j)} f → ∫_{T_xN_j} f, and the vanishing of the two error integrals. Here M ↦ A, N_j ↦ N, M_j ↦ A ∩ N, so N_j∖M_j = N∖A and M∖M_j = A∖N; with this identification the documented erratum (the printed proof estimates 'M∖N_j' where its decomposition needs M∖M_j and N_j∖M_j) is moot, and the two error sets are exactly the sets whose zero-density hypotheses are assumed.

Notation. μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ; B_ρ(y) is the closed ball; η_r := η_{x,r} = Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x); 'r ↓ 0' means along 𝓝[>] 0; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal. Sibling (V) = aetp_blowUp_integral_tendsto_zero_of_density_zero: for every set S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with μ(S ∩ B_s(x))/ofReal(sⁿ) → 0 as s ↓ 0 and every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ), ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ → 0 as r ↓ 0.

Proof.
1. Dimension. The hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q contains finrank Q = n, which is the first component of the conclusion. For the second component fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ); we must show ∫_{η_r(A)} f dμ → ∫_Q f dμ as r ↓ 0.
2. Limits of the pieces. By the second component of the hypothesis on N, ∫_{η_r(N)} f dμ → ∫_Q f dμ. By (V) with S := A∖N and the first density hypothesis, ∫_{η_r(A∖N)} f dμ → 0. By (V) with S := N∖A and the second density hypothesis, ∫_{η_r(N∖A)} f dμ → 0. By the algebra of limits in ℝ, ∫_{η_r(N)} f dμ − ∫_{η_r(N∖A)} f dμ + ∫_{η_r(A∖N)} f dμ → ∫_Q f dμ − 0 + 0 = ∫_Q f dμ.
3. Reduction. The set (0, ∞) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0, so by Tendsto.congr' it suffices that the two functions of r agree for every r > 0, i.e. to prove, for every fixed r > 0, the identity
 (∗) ∫_{η_r(A)} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(N)} f dμ − ∫_{η_r(N∖A)} f dμ + ∫_{η_r(A∖N)} f dμ.
 Fix r > 0.
4. η_r is a homeomorphism. η_r is continuous with continuous inverse y ↦ x + r·y (r ≠ 0); hence it is a measurable embedding: injective, and images of measurable sets are measurable. So η_r(A∖N) and η_r(N∖A) are measurable (A∖N and N∖A are Borel). Injectivity gives disjoint images: η_r(A∩N) ∩ η_r(A∖N) = ∅ and η_r(A∩N) ∩ η_r(N∖A) = ∅. Since A = (A∩N) ∪ (A∖N), N = (A∩N) ∪ (N∖A), and images commute with unions, η_r(A) = η_r(A∩N) ∪ η_r(A∖N) and η_r(N) = η_r(A∩N) ∪ η_r(N∖A).
5. Finite measure. For every T ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, μ(η_r(T)) = ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ · μ(T): η_r is the homothety with center 0 and ratio r⁻¹ composed with the isometry y ↦ y − x; isometries preserve μ (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and the homothety multiplies μ by ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ = ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). (This is SimonGMT Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_image, re-derived because Chapter04 is outside the frozen import closure.) By monotonicity μ(A∩N) ≤ μ(A) < ∞, μ(A∖N) ≤ μ(A) < ∞ and μ(N∖A) ≤ μ(N) < ∞; as ofReal(r⁻¹)ⁿ < ∞, the sets η_r(A∩N), η_r(A∖N), η_r(N∖A) have finite μ-measure.
6. Integrability. f is continuous, hence (AE-)strongly measurable, and, being continuous with compact support, bounded: |f| ≤ C for some C (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). A bounded AE-strongly measurable function is integrable on every set of finite measure (IntegrableOn.of_bound). Hence f is μ-integrable on η_r(A∩N), η_r(A∖N) and η_r(N∖A).
7. Additivity. By additivity of the Bochner set integral over a disjoint union whose second set is measurable and on both parts of which f is integrable (setIntegral_union), steps 4–6 give
 ∫_{η_r(A)} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(A∩N)} f dμ + ∫_{η_r(A∖N)} f dμ and ∫_{η_r(N)} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(A∩N)} f dμ + ∫_{η_r(N∖A)} f dμ.
 Eliminating ∫_{η_r(A∩N)} f dμ yields (∗).
